extracted.intended_audience: external peer reviewers, expert panel members, and researchers applying for Cancer Research UK funding
extracted.subtask_short: CRUK peer review of grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for external expert reviewers on how Cancer Research UK assesses funding applications, including the criteria reviewers should consider and expected reviewer conduct. Intended to steer review comments that feed into funding committee decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: scientific excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed as one of the general criteria by which peer reviewers assess applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the overall scientific quality of the proposal — novelty, rigor, clarity of hypotheses and objectives, appropriateness of methods, and potential to advance knowledge. (Implicitly connected to statements elsewhere on the page about ensuring scientific rigour.)

rubrics_metrics.name: cancer relevance and impact on the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are assessed for their relevance to cancer and the potential impact on the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how clearly the proposal addresses cancer-related problems and the magnitude/importance of the expected impact on cancer research, prevention, diagnosis, or treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: team and research environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should consider the composition of the research team and the suitability of the research environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the investigators and their institutional setting provide the appropriate expertise, mentorship, facilities and support to deliver the project successfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: resources requested
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the resources and budget requested in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the requested funds and resources are appropriate, justified, and economical for the proposed work; consider whether costs match the scale and aims of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: previous research outputs and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the applicants' past outputs and their expertise relative to the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use track record (publications, prior grants, relevant experience) to assess the team's ability to deliver the proposed research and whether expertise gaps exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: whether sharing of outputs is consistent with best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the applicants plan to share outputs (data, code, materials) in ways consistent with best practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider plans for dissemination, data and resource sharing, and whether these will maximise reuse, reproducibility, and benefit to the research community. (Linked to the page's emphasis on how outputs will be shared to generate more great science.)

rubrics_metrics.name: quality of the research
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlighted as a key principle reviewers are encouraged to consider (used alongside translation and sharing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge scientific rigour, methodological robustness, feasibility and clarity of the research plan — essentially overlapping with 'scientific excellence' but emphasised as a core guiding principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: potential for translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Review whether the proposed research has potential to translate into meaningful clinical, diagnostic, prevention or policy outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the plausibility and pathway for translation, including relevance to patient benefit, implementation considerations, and the likelihood of moving from discovery to application.

rubrics_metrics.name: how outputs will be shared within the research community
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of plans for dissemination and sharing as part of generating more great science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine proposed dissemination strategies (publications, data repositories, open access, code sharing, collaborations) and how they support reuse and community impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: scientific rigour (ensure scientific rigour of projects funded)
rubrics_metrics.description: The funder uses a multi-tiered peer review to ensure scientific rigour of projects it funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess methodological soundness, appropriate controls, statistical plans, reproducibility measures, and risk mitigation strategies within the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: alignment with our strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the proposal aligns with Cancer Research UK's research strategy and priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider strategic fit — whether the work advances areas the funder prioritises and contributes to the organisation's stated aims for understanding, preventing, detecting or treating cancer.

rubrics_metrics.name: engage the most appropriate reviewers (reviewer selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: The funder aims to engage reviewers who are competitive researchers with expertise relevant to the applicant’s proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer selection is based on topical expertise and standing; reviews should therefore reflect domain-appropriate judgement and comparative perspective against field standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: declare any potential conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviewers are asked to declare any potential conflicts of interest before carrying out peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must disclose relationships or circumstances that could bias their assessment; conflicts should be reported and handled according to the funder's guidance to ensure impartiality of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: treat application content as confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must treat all information in applications as confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share, disclose or use application content outside the review process; follow the funder's confidentiality agreement and procedures for protecting sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: prohibition on using generative AI with application content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers sign a confidentiality agreement promising not to enter, input or disclose any content from funding applications into generative AI tools; or use generative AI tools in drafting, formulating or editing peer review critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not copy-paste application text into AI models or use AI to draft/edit review comments for these applications; adhere to the funder's specific policy on generative AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: expectation that funded researchers participate in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The funder expects all its funded researchers to participate in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being a funded researcher implies a reciprocal duty to contribute to peer review panels/committees when requested, supporting the wider funding ecosystem.
